decision: Primary model `Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B` @ `851bf6e8…`, BF16, single GPU, greedy, `enable_thinking=False`, `max_new_tokens=32`, batch 1
rationale: the design assessment protocol.

decision: Candidate order key = `sha256("fatima-evidence-2026-v1:" + str(image_id))`, ascending
rationale: the design assessment protocol (verbatim).

decision: A/B assignment bit = `int(sha256("fatima-evidence-2026-v1:ab-assignment:" + id), 16) & 1`; bit 0 → A is the person whose box centre is further left (ties: lower annotation id)
rationale: the design assessment requires "a hash-derived fair bit" but does not give the salt. Fixed before any annotation.

decision: Robustness subset = the first 20 selected held-out items by `sha256("fatima-evidence-2026-v1:robustness:" + id)`. The pilot marks 5 items to exercise the tag-reversal path
rationale: the design assessment requires selection by image-ID hash, not failures. The salt is fixed here, before inference.

decision: Automatic size pre-screen: both COCO person boxes must be ≥ 48×48 px on the canvas before human review; failures are never shown as eligible
rationale: A strictly necessary consequence of criterion 5 (a garment cannot exceed its person's box). It removes no scene that could pass. val2017: 158 of 293 pass.

decision: Markers: box = person box expanded by 3 px, drawn as 4 one-pixel strokes (black, white, white, black); tag = white rectangle with a black letter in Pillow's embedded font at size 22, placed above the top-left corner (fallbacks: below, then inside)
rationale: the design assessment: "thin black/white outlined person boxes and A/B tags outside the body evidence". Exact geometry was unspecified.

decision: Isolation diagnostic = gray canvas plus the target's canvas box pixels (clean canvas, rounded outward, clipped to the content box) at the same coordinates, with only the target's marker. The user prompt is unchanged
rationale: the design assessment Section V.6. Keeping the prompt identical keeps the diagnostic comparable, though its "two people are marked" phrase is then counterfactual. Reported as a diagnostic only.

decision: Shams must stay at least 12 px from each person box (34 px above and below for tag zones), inside the photographic content (not the padding), and disjoint from all masks. The tool proposes the nearest such location; a human confirms it
rationale: A sham on padding would be a no-op edit, and a sham touching a marker would hide part of the applied mask. The renderer independently checks disjointness, the content box, person-box exclusion and marker overlap.

decision: Rater stage 2 shows I01 to rater 1 and I10 to rater 2
rationale: the design assessment Section V.4: "assignment reversed between reviewers".

decision: Confirmatory items need both raters to pass and agree on both colours; colours then come from the raters. Exploratory mode also admits author-only scenes, labelled `exploratory_single_rater`
rationale: the design assessment Section V.4: a single annotator is exploratory.

decision: GPU smoke test uses 5 train2017 (pilot-split) photographs with engineering placeholder masks (rectangles at 25–75% width and 22–50% height of each person box), placeholder colours black/white, and `annotation_status=engineering_placeholder_not_human`. They are never analysed
rationale: the design assessment requires a smoke test on pilot images before the pilot. Human masks did not yet exist, and the smoke test measures only technical properties.

decision: Work data (manifests, annotations, renders, predictions, results) live in `work_root` outside Git; the release staging copies the publishable subset
rationale: Keeps images and large files out of version control.

decision: Parser accepts one surrounding ```` ```json\n … \n``` ```` fence (`allow_json_fence: true`); nothing else is normalised
rationale: GPU smoke test (5 pilot photos, placeholder masks, 68 queries): 46/68 answers were fenced JSON, so strict-only parsing gave 22/68 valid. With the fence accepted, 65/68 are valid. The 3 invalid outputs used the tag as key (`{"A": "UNKNOWN"}`) and stay invalid. the design assessment allows a fence normalisation if it is fixed in the pilot. Decided on format only, before any annotated pilot outcome. The 95.6% valid rate is below the 99% gate; the pilot decides whether a single prompt revision is needed.

decision: **Time-boxed pilot**: pilot-pool candidates are examined in order until 8 author-eligible scenes or 30 minutes of screening, whichever comes first. Proceed with ≥ 5; with fewer, proceed and record the shortfall
rationale: Deviation from the design assessment's planned 20-scene pilot, forced by the submission deadline (07:59 EDT) and a single available annotator. Pilot gate estimates will be correspondingly imprecise.

decision: **Amendment A01**: val2017 stays the original evaluation cohort (exhausted in order, exploratory if single-rater). A separate prospective replication cohort is defined on the 3,789 unused size-feasible train2017 candidates (ranks ≥ 555), disjoint from the 300-image pilot pool, stopping at 80 two-rater clusters. **No pooling.** Internal hash-locked amendment, not an external preregistration. See `docs/amendments/A01_train2017_extension/`
rationale: The AI-only feasibility audit suggests val2017 cannot reach 80 eligible clusters. the design assessment allows a separately preregistered train2017 replication. Recorded with zero annotations and zero val2017 or pilot outputs.

decision: **SAM-HQ point-prompt assistance** for garment masks: the author clicks garment (+) and non-garment (−) points; SAM-HQ ViT-L (`sam_hq_vit_l.pth`, sha256 `e1a6c385d62bf005ded91a54d5ec55c985cfc4103ef89c08d90f39f04934c343`, SysCV/sam-hq commit `e696978`) proposes a mask, which is converted to polygons (outer contours, holes filled, RDP 1 px, specks < 64 px dropped). The author accepts, edits or redraws it. Every person record stores `mask_source` (`manual` or `sam_assisted`), `edited_after_sam` and the full SAM provenance (points, labels, score, model hash). Colours remain human-only
rationale: Requested by the applicant before any annotation existed, so all cohorts use the same tool. the design assessment allows automatic segmentation to assist the mask author but not to replace human verification. The staged rater audit and the render checks still decide evidence-removal adequacy. SAM is independent of the evaluated VLM and never sees colours, gold labels or model outputs. Manual polygons remain available as a fallback.

decision: **Marker box encloses the garment mask.** Each person's outline box is the union of the COCO box (expanded by 3 px) and that person's dilated garment mask (expanded by 5 px). The 4-px outline therefore stays at least 1 px clear of the person's own mask. The sham keep-out (tool and automatic proposer) uses the same enlarged box
rationale: Found before any pilot render or inference: SAM-assisted masks routinely reach the tight COCO box edge, so the original outline was drawn over the dilated mask and violated the design assessment's rule that markers must not cover garment evidence. 2 of 3 dry-run pilot scenes failed `marker_keepout`; after the change both render PASS. Flagged first by the VAW integration spike. Tests: `tests/test_marker_extent.py`, plus a replacement marker-violation test.

decision: **Pilot executed under D-014 with a shortfall.** One author (single rater). 21 pilot-pool scenes were examined, but not in strict order: 29 ranks ≤ 82 were skipped (`selection_flow_pilot.json` and author records list them). 8 were marked eligible; the renderer's automatic checks rejected 5 (4 garment size, 1 overlapping masks), leaving **3 pilot scenes** (44 queries, 0 technical errors). Pilot gates: clean 0.83 FAIL, isolated 0.83 FAIL, sham drop 0.00 PASS, valid JSON 0.917 FAIL
rationale: The time box was reached. The pilot is design-only and never enters estimates. Out-of-order screening is a deviation acceptable for the pilot. It is **not** acceptable for val2017, which must be examined strictly in order. No revision decision has been taken yet.

decision: New render check `garment_inside_own_box_{A,B}`: at least 50% of each person's undilated garment mask must lie inside that person's COCO box
rationale: Scene 537371 had its two polygons saved under the wrong persons (0% inside own box), which only an unrelated overlap check happened to catch. After re-rendering, all pilot images are byte-identical (verified), so the pilot queries and outputs remain valid; the 3 PASS scenes score 0.995–1.0.

decision: **Protocol frozen as 1.0-frozen, with no pilot revision.** Prompts, parser (with D-013), generation settings, renderer (D-017, D-019), annotation tool (D-016), analysis code and the val2017 candidate manifest are hash-locked in `docs/protocol_freeze/1.0-frozen/`. val2017 is then annotated strictly in order by a single author (exploratory) until the time limit, and the last examined rank is recorded
rationale: The pilot (3 scenes) failed three gates (clean 0.83, isolated 0.83, valid JSON 0.917), each decided by one or two responses. A revision justified at n=3, and re-tested on fresh train2017 images, would leave no time for held-out data before the deadline. Under the design assessment's rules, a pilot that does not pass means **no GO for the confirmatory interpretation**: the val2017 result is reported as exploratory, and the failed gates are disclosed.

decision: **Amendment A02**: renderer inclusion screen 32×32/900 px², with nested analysis cohorts original (48/2304), moderate (40/1500) and expanded (32/900) computed from the same outputs. All other rules unchanged. Exploratory
rationale: Applicant-approved and pilot-informed: garments fill 50–71% of their box. Recorded before any val2017 inference.

decision: **Execution record (end of session).** val2017: ranks 1–8 examined in order (5 author records; ranks 3–5 not size-feasible): 1 eligible (372819), 2 unsure, 2 reject. 372819 renders PASS but fails the 48/2304 original cohort (A area 1728); 20 held-out queries, 0 errors. AI visual inspection of I00 shows **incomplete evidence removal** (A's jacket hem and an orange fragment of B remain visible) and an open multicolour jacket for B; the model answered each hidden target's own colour 4/4 times. The scene needs the human rater audit and is expected to be rejected or re-masked. Pilot re-run under A02 (`pilot_qwen35_A02`, 5 scenes, 84 queries) reproduced all 44 earlier outputs exactly
rationale: Records actual state; no labels were changed. Held-out estimates from this single, likely invalid scene must not be interpreted.
